note:
Malcolm, 2026-08-24: use pdrn-skin-repair-serum--C-face-full-eyes-open-left gpt_image_01 as homepage hero slide 3, but fix the bottle first — 'the bottle and the text should be correct'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH THE BOTTLE. Compared against the product's own hero shot, __pdrn_skin_repair_deep_renewal_face_serum_hero_white_bg_8: the frame renders a slim narrow bottle with a short collar, where the real product is a WIDE straight-sided bottle with square shoulders and a tall brushed satin aluminium collar. On the label the wordmark, PDRN and SKIN REPAIR are right, but the thin vertical rose rule is absent, TREATMENT is missing from under DEEP RENEWAL, and PREMIUM FORMULA and the dosage line are absent entirely.

THE MISSING LINES WERE ASKED FOR, NOT FUMBLED. The banner-library brief said in terms that only four lines should be legible and 'every remaining line falls outside the depth of field'. That is right for a library banner and wrong for a hero, so the label is now quoted in full, verbatim, with the colour of each line stated — an invented label survives review, a garbled one does not.

WHY THE ORIGINAL COULD NOT HAVE CARRIED THE FULL LABEL. gpt-image caps its long edge at 2048, which left this bottle about 165px wide and its label about 150px. Four short lines fit in that budget; seven do not. Nano Banana generates at 6336px, where the same 8% of frame width is over 500px of label — enough for the letters to be formed correctly before any downscale. This is the identical lesson to the hero label fixed earlier today: resolution at the moment of generation, not sharpening afterwards.

THE HEADLINE COLLISION — the reason there are three variants. All three hero slides carry desktop_text_position 'sm:place-self-center-start', i.e. the headline sits centre-LEFT. This frame puts the bottle and hand in the left third. Measured on a 6x3 grid, the left-middle cells run mean 59-80 with stdev 48-61, which is busy, bright and hostile to white type; the only clean region is the top-right at mean 20-21, stdev 1-11. A left-aligned headline would sit straight on the bottle. So:
  * A-FAITHFUL keeps Malcolm's composition exactly and needs the slide's text moved to the top right.
  * B-BIGGER keeps the composition but brings the bottle up in scale for a label that reads at render size; same text-position consequence.
  * C-LEFTCLEAR moves the subject right and holds the left third dark graphite, so the headline stays where slides 1 and 2 put it and nothing in the theme changes.
That choice is Malcolm's, not mine, which is why all three are generated rather than one being picked for him.

SUPPLIER NOTES. Class A with legible branding, so FLUX.2 is barred. Luma is reference-blind here and has refused this subject family all session; it is still attempted per rule 1. Generated at the hero's own 3072x1368 aspect so no crop is needed later.

slots.title: Malcolm's frame, composition untouched, bottle and label corrected
slots.prompt: Take the first reference photograph and change only the bottle. Everything else stays exactly as it is: the same woman lying with her head resting on one side, the same level composed gaze straight into the lens, her whole face in view and sharp, the same wet-look dark hair swept back, the same bare shoulder and neck running away to the right, the same real unretouched skin with visible pores and freckles, the same deep graphite background, the same single directional light from above, the same framing with the bottle held in her hand in the left third of the picture and clear of her face. Do not re-pose her, do not re-light her, do not smooth her skin, do not move the hand or the bottle. Replace the bottle in her hand with the exact bottle shown in the second reference image, matching it in every respect: a 30ml frosted ROSE-PINK glass dropper bottle, WIDE and straight-sided with square shoulders and a broad flat base, noticeably chunky rather than slim, fitted with a TALL brushed satin aluminium collar about a third of the height of the glass body, and a white rubber-bulb pipette above it. The rose-pink is the colour of the GLASS ITSELF; the serum inside is clear, colourless and water-transparent, and the pipette stem shows through the glass. Reproduce the front label exactly as in the second reference, every character verbatim, in this order, with these colours: the Skingenetix DNA double-helix mark in black at the top, the wordmark 'Skingenetix' in bold black beneath it, then a thin vertical rose-pink rule down the left of the text block, and beside that rule 'PDRN' and 'SKIN REPAIR' in bold black capitals on two lines, 'DEEP RENEWAL' and 'TREATMENT' in bold rose-pink capitals on two lines, 'PREMIUM FORMULA' in plain black capitals, and at the foot '1% (10,000 PPM) PDRN | 30ML' in small black capitals. Do not add, remove, reorder or restyle any word. The label is turned square to camera, is the plane of focus and the sharpest thing in the picture, every character crisply edged and fully legible at full resolution down to the smallest line, lines evenly spaced and straight on the glass. Her fingers stay clear of the lettering.
